messages:
maria (oncall): incident-bot fired: slo_burn_high for /generate, 10m window 3.2x burn. Paging us.
incident-bot: ALERT: slo_burn_high on service=redwood-api route=/v1/generate window=10m burn=3.2x severity=page
maria (oncall): I'm looking at traces now, tailing the proxy logs. Early sign: surge from a single customer IP range.
adev: can you paste the proxy sample? any 5xxs?
maria (oncall): small spike in 502 and a lot of long tail latency. pasted logs:
```
2026-07-12T14:22:03Z proxy svc request_id=abc123 route=/v1/generate status=502 latency=11000ms client=35.190.12.0/24
2026-07-12T14:22:04Z proxy svc request_id=abc124 route=/v1/generate status=200 latency=12000ms client=35.190.12.0/24
```
jen: surprising to see many 200s but high latency — probably slow model backend, not an outright crash.
tim: I see model pool CPU at 98% and many queued tokens. Likely batching backpressure.
sre-ops: is this across regions or single region? metrics show us-west-2 only.
adev: can we temporarily reroute that customer's traffic to a lower-capacity variant or slower batching to avoid SLO burn? we have a fallback policy but need to trigger it.
maria (oncall): initiating canary fallback to v1-quantized variant now. will update once routing rule applied.
incident-bot: ACTION: routing.fallback applied for customer cid=acme-corp -> model=rwx-small-quantized
maria (oncall): fallback applied at 14:27Z. initial effect: p95 latency dropped from 9.8s -> 2.4s for that cid.
jen: good. what's our customer impact? page the account team?
maria (oncall): partial impact: yes — increased tails for that CID but overall SLO trending down. I'm prepping a short blurb for account.
adev: we should adjust paging thresholds to reduce chatter for noisy single-customer bursts. Current policy pages at 2x burn over 10m. Suggest change: require at least 2 affected customer sessions OR burn >4x for single-customer before paging.
tim: agree. also multi-window logic: 10m is okay for immediate pages but our burn alerting for broader ops should check 30m window too. propose dual-window alert:
- page if burn>=3x in 10m and impacted_sessions>=2
- or page if burn>=5x in 10m
- or notify if burn>=2x in 30m (no page)
jen: sounds reasonable. we should also create a dashboard tile that breaks burn by customer CID and by model variant.
sre-ops: I'll add a grafana panel: slo_burn_by_cid and variant. putting a draft query here:
```
sum by (cid) (rate(slo_burn_total{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) / sum(rate(slo_budget_total{route="/v1/generate"}[5m]))
```
maria (oncall): action item: jen please notify account for acme-corp with brief timeline and that fallback was used. jen: ack.
adev: action item: tim and sre-ops, update alert rules and add multi-window variant. include test alerts to #eng-sre-sandbox.
tim: on it. I'll push a PR with the three-rule logic and a short rationale in the PR description.
jen: I'll draft the customer-facing note. recommend: 1) what happened 2) what we did 3) mitigation and next steps (playbook update + post-incident follow-up).
maria (oncall): playbook update: add a decision point to prefer model fallback for single-customer bursts and include threshold numbers above.
incident-bot: NOTE: Incident created: INC-2026-5647, severity=SEV3, assigned=eng-sre
sre-ops: postmortem owner? I'm volunteering to lead the RCA because it's tied to batching heuristics.
adev: sgtm. include evals team to run load tests on rwx-small-quantized to ensure quality hasn't regressed.
jen: we'll need to update our post-incident dashboard to show token cost delta for fallbacks — ops wants to understand cost impact of automatic fallback.
maria (oncall): last check: slo burn down to 1.1x across windows after fallback and additional autoscale (scaled model pool by +2). continuing to monitor.
adev: nice. timeline for alert rule change? tim, can you aim to have PR by EOD and test tomorrow morning?
tim: EOD PR, tests tomorrow.
sre-ops: I'll create the grafana panel and a temporary runbook section in the playbook repo: "Single-customer surge -> prefer fallback -> assess quality -> if quality OK, keep until load subsides".
maria (oncall): thanks all. I'll update the incident page with these notes and close the page when burn stays <1.2x for 2 hours.
jen: pinging account team: @accounts acme-corp got a fallback on 2026-07-12T14:27Z. Please expect a follow-up from Jen.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: INC-2026-5647 status=monitoring
maria (oncall): any objections to the alert wording change? if none, we'll proceed with the PR as discussed.
adev: no objections.
tim: no objections.
jen: no objections.
sre-ops: no objections. documenting now.
maria (oncall): ending thread for now — will reopen if burn increases. :white_check_mark:
